entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6304"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 73</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.73.1-Ps.73.28">Psa 73:1-28</reference>. Of Asaph--(see Introduction). God is good to His people. For although the prosperity of the wicked, and the afflictions of the righteous, tempted the Psalmist to misgivings of God's government, yet the sudden and fearful ruin of the ungodly, seen in the light of God's revelation, reassures his heart; and, chiding himself for his folly, he is led to confide renewedly in God, and celebrate His goodness and love.</title> <div sID="gen9656" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6304"/>1. The abrupt announcement of the theme indicates that it is the conclusion of a perplexing mental conflict, which is then detailed (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.12.1-Jer.12.4">Jr 12:1-4</reference>).<div eID="gen9656" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9657" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Truly--</hi>or, "Surely it is so."<div eID="gen9657" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9658" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">clean heart--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.18.26">Psa 18:26</reference>) describes the true Israel. <div eID="gen9658" type="x-p"/>

Truly-- or, "Surely it is so." clean heart-- ( Psa 18:26 ) describes the true Israel.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6314"/><div sID="gen9671" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6314"/><hi type="bold">18-20. their end--</hi>future (<reference osisRef="Ps.37.37">Psa 37:37</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.37.38">38</reference>), which is dismal and terribly sudden (<reference osisRef="Prov.1.27">Pr 1:27</reference>; 29:1), aggravated and hastened by terror. As one despises an unsubstantial dream, so God, waking up to judgment (<reference osisRef="Ps.7.6">Psa 7:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.44.23">44:23</reference>), despises their vain shadow of happiness (<reference osisRef="Ps.39.6">Psa 39:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.29.7">Is 29:7</reference>). They are thrown into ruins as a building falling to pieces (<reference osisRef="Ps.74.3">Psa 74:3</reference>). <div eID="gen9671" type="x-p"/>
